newsitem.title: USA: Motorola Q2 earnings seen up from Q1.
newsitem.headline: Motorola Q2 earnings seen up from Q1.

text.p: Motorola Inc, benefitting from what appears to be a resurgence in its key industries, is expected to show earnings have grown slightly from the first quarter's $0.53 a share and last year's $0.54, analysts said.
"I think the momentum is in the second half, but I bet the second quarter will be operationally better than the first," said Gruntal & Co analyst Mona Eraiba. "That's my key bet."

The Schaumburg, Ill.-based technology giant has suffered a downturn in its key semiconductor business and stiff competition in the cellular phone sector. Motorola is one of the first technology companies to report earnings, scheduled for Tuesday after the market closes, and analysts said they will look for signs that a talked-about turnaround is solidly underway in both industries.

According to First Call, the consensus of analysts' estimates is $0.56 a share. The estimates exclude a $170 million pretax charge the company said it will take for its exit from the DRAM (dynamic random access memory) chip market.

Revenues of about $7 billion are expected, versus last year's $6.83 billion. In first quarter 1997, Motorola reported earnings of $0.53 a share on revenues of $6.6 billion. Motorola declined to comment, citing company policy.

The company's semicondutor products segment returned to profitability in the first quarter with sales of $1.8 billion, and analysts said they will look for continued improvement. In the second quarter last year, Motorola reported semiconductor group sales of $2.0 billion.

Although various computer technology companies have cautioned about weaker-than-anticipated demand, analysts said Motorola's chips are used more in cellular phones and products other than personal computers.
"The quarter is also going to be driven by semiconductors," said Cowen & Co analyst Wojtek Uzdelewicz.
Most analysts said they expect to see improvement in Motorola's cellular subscriber sector, which includes cellular phones. Analysts said prices appear to be stabilizing.

After being late to market with some higher-margin digital phones, new products have been released. In addition, the Star-Tac wireless phone, a miniature, wearable handset, has been well accepted in the market, they said.
"They're really doing well with new products, particularly in the digital cellular area," Montgomery Securities analyst John Joseph said.
The cellular segment, which includes both phones and infrastructure, posted first quarter sales of $2.7 billion.
On Monday, shares of Motorola traded up 1-3/16 at 81-5/8.
